To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DA transporter inhibitor GBR12909 enhances the long‐duration response of levodopa in patients with Parkinson's disease, that GBR12909‐induced enhancement of the long‐duration effect of levodopa depends on DA release, and that GBR12939‐induced enhancement is mediated by D1 and D2 receptors.
the long‐duration response of levodopa on the performance of a motor task is mediated by dopamine‐dependent learning.
the dopamine transporter (DAT) is a target of the antipsychotic drugs (APDs) and is a target of psychostimulant drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of levodopa on motor learning and the mechanisms underlying them, and the relationship between motor performance, motor skill learning and dopamine (DA) neurotransmission.
the effects of dopamine on learning and memory, and the mechanisms underlying these effects.
the role of dopamine in the mediation of motor learning and the long-term effects of levodopa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DA system is critical in the mediation of motor learning, and the DAergic system in the striatum is a key component of this mediation.
the dopamine system has a role in learning and memory.

DA is critical for both motor performance and learning; however, the precise mechanisms underlying the DA‐mediated modulation of motor learning and the relationship between motor learning and motor performance remain elusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DA plays a key role in motor performance and motor learning and that DA is required for the long‐duration response of levodopa.
the long‐lasting response of levodopa on motor learning and performance is dependent on DA release.
the DAergic system is critical for motor learning, which is reflected by the long duration response of levodopa in patients with Parkinson's disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DA plays a critical role in the mediation of motor performance and learning.
the motor learning process can be broken down into two phases: a short‐term, dopamine‐independent phase, and a long‐term, dopamine ‐dependent phase.
DA‐dependent motor learning and motor performance are separable processes.
